name: CA-32
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+14 district partisanship anchors the seat in Democratic territory
Sherman holds a massive money edge: $2.7M cash on hand vs. about $2K for Thompson
Longtime incumbent running with no meaningful outside spending against him
Prediction markets price the race near 96% Democratic despite no public polling
model.rationale: The district's 14-point Democratic lean, Sherman's incumbency, and a lopsided resource gap — $2.7 million on hand against roughly $2,000 for his opponent — leave virtually no path for an upset, and markets price the race near 96 percent Democratic.
model.watch: Only a sudden wave of outside spending against Sherman or an unforeseen scandal could narrow the race; otherwise the only open question is the size of the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 32nd District, centered in the San Fernando Valley, leans strongly Democratic with a 14-point partisan edge. Brad Sherman, the longtime incumbent, advanced to the general election and faces Republican Larry Thompson, who has run a minimal campaign. Sherman has raised about $2.5 million and holds $2.7 million on hand, while Thompson has raised roughly $34,000 and reported just over $2,000 in cash. No outside groups are opposing Sherman in meaningful terms.

No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have listed it, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Prediction markets put Sherman's chances near 96 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a vast resource gap makes this one of the safest Democratic holds on the House map, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
